observation.visible_scene: A tranquil, slow-moving forest stream or pond framed by dense green summer foliage on both banks, with a pale sky visible through a gap in the canopy. The calm foreground water mirrors the trees and sky. A single light-colored rock breaks the surface left of center, a fallen log/branch lies along the right bank, and several out-of-focus lens-flare dots (green upper-left, orange mid-left) are overlaid on the image.
visible_changes: The water surface shows only subtle, continuous ripple/shimmer motion: the reflected tree trunks and the bright sky patch in the foreground waver and deform slightly from frame to frame, with no large translation of the reflected image.

All solid scene elements—the protruding rock, the right-bank log, the tree canopy, the sky gap—and the fixed lens-flare dots stay in the same pixel positions across the excerpt, indicating a stationary camera and no moving objects, animals, or people.
Lighting and color remain constant; there is no visible onset, contact, or completion of any action within the segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the faint surface ripples (wind, current, or an unseen disturbance) is not shown.
Whether any object or motion enters or leaves the scene before the first frame or after the last frame is unknown, since both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
uncertain_details: Any very slight leaf sway in the canopy is not clearly resolvable at this resolution.
The precise phase/looping of the ripple pattern cannot be determined from a temporally cropped excerpt.
